messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: RC7 Changes
parts:
You can use the javax.script API for this. Take a look at:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/script-engine/src/test/java/org/renjin/script/RenjinScriptEngineTest.java

to see how to invoke an R function and cast the result to the corresponding Java class. A data.frame in R is actually just a list with the class attribute "data.frame", so in Java-land, you can cast the result of a function that returns a data.frame to an instanceof org.renjin.sexp.ListVector.

The columns of the data.frame are elements within the ListVector, which you can access in java by x.getElementAsSexp(columnIndex). All data.frame columns should be instances of org.renjin.sexp.AtomicVector (the super class of IntVector, DoubleVector, StringVector, etc), which has methods that will allow you to access the individual elements (e.g. getElementAsDouble, getElementAsInt)

Note that factors in R are just IntVectors with a class "factor" and a "levels" attribute which provides labels for the integer values.

Thanks for checking it out, and yet another reminder that we *really* need to finish the java developer's guide!

Best,
Alex

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: RC7 Changes
parts:
Do you mean the row names? those are stored as an attribute. You can access this in java using:

StringVector names = (StringVector)df.getAttribute("row.names")

Columm names are in the "names" attribute, btw.

If you mean row data, there are no actual rows, as the data.frame stores its data as columns. So to get the value at row 5, column 2, you could say:

df.getElementAsSexp(2).getElementAsDouble(5)

there may be a cast missing...

hth,
Alex
